results.description: system-ERTS startup latency + fixed compute loop
allocate-and-abandon garbage churn under each runtime (per-op GC cost)
notes: staged $TMPDIR/bench-scratch-gc_bound-3614-0-1793105951721928199/bench_gc_bound.beam (embedded source, LEN=256, per-op increment=1, erlc=/nix/store/lljrlcd2cqv64a6xz4cyaz723x2nwpnl-erlang-29.1.2/lib/erlang/erts-17.1.1/bin/erlc)
case churn: paired median=849.219 ms min=848.097 ms max=872.209 ms noise=±1.664 ms over 3 round(s)
observed stdout: churn=N*1=200000
case churn: N=200000 churns (sys), each allocating and abandoning a 256-element list, a 256-byte binary and a 256-element tuple

method: every round runs the program at N churns and then at 0 churns back to back, and ns/op is the median paired difference (wall@N - wall@0) / N * 1e6 — never two separate means, whose difference absorbs a drifting boot cost instead of cancelling it. N is per runtime so both marginals are measurable, the fixed process startup (incl. the Rust runtime's code-path resolution) cancels inside every pair, and a figure inside the noise band is withheld rather than published

note: the op count is deterministic and contention-immune; the wall-clock rows move with host load. Whether a runtime's collector actually runs during the loop is its own admission policy — this row measures the allocate-and-abandon wall time, and claims no collection count

results.description: a BIF-free recursive list walk on both runtimes (interpreter ns/element)
notes: staged $TMPDIR/bench-scratch-list_walk-3614-2-1793105962346009212/bench_list_walk.beam (embedded source, LEN=1000, erlc=/nix/store/lljrlcd2cqv64a6xz4cyaz723x2nwpnl-erlang-29.1.2/lib/erlang/erts-17.1.1/bin/erlc)
case list_walk: paired median=225.668 ms min=221.858 ms max=225.802 ms noise=±1.000 ms over 3 round(s)
observed stdout: list_walk=N*500500=50050000000
case list_walk: N=100000 walks (sys) at LEN=1000, i.e. 100000000 elements walked

method: paired startup-cancelled marginal — every round runs the N-walk pass then the 0-walk pass back to back, and ns/element = median(paired difference) / (N * LEN) * 1e6, withheld below 3x max(1 ms, 1.4826*MAD) of the paired differences; N is per runtime so both marginals are measurable, and the fixed process startup (incl. the Rust runtime's code-path resolution) cancels inside every pair; the module is BIF-free and builds no term
note: element count is deterministic and contention-immune; the wall-clock rows move with host load

budgets.reason: no `rust` row for `baseline` in this report (that runtime was not selected, or is unsupported here)
budgets.rationale: A gross-regression alarm for the Rust boot median (the six m19 matched rounds read 260.3-261.4 ms at a 1-min load of 0.5-4.5; m17's loaded rounds read 289-546 ms at load 3-92), not an SLO — a shared host can double it without a code change, so the load-robust judgement is the rust/sys ratio row.

budgets.rationale: Catches a hang or an order-of-magnitude tail regression (the six m19 matched rounds read 261.9-267.6 ms p99; m17 read up to 485 ms, with a single 1702 ms outlier on a heavily loaded A/B round), not an SLO: a boot's p99 is a handful of samples, so this row only notices a gross failure.

budgets.reason: no `rust` row for `baseline` in this report (that runtime was not selected, or is unsupported here)
budgets.rationale: The load-robust startup judgement: the six m19 matched rounds read 2.51-2.53x (m16 reached 3.79x), so 6x is a regression alarm with headroom above every recorded round — not a target, and deliberately not so tight that ordinary host drift trips it.

budgets.reason: no `rust` row for `baseline` in this report (that runtime was not selected, or is unsupported here)
budgets.rationale: The same instrument for the tail; the p99 ratios track the p50 ones (2.35-2.58x across the six m19 matched rounds) because a boot's p99 is a handful of samples, so the same 6x alarm applies — not an SLO for a shared host.

The oracle's own tail, recorded at 103.5-113.3 ms across the six m19 matched rounds (m17 read 105-153 ms): a host artifact big enough to move the far less load-sensitive `sys` side shows up here too, so it cannot be misread as a Rust regression — and 400 ms is deliberately loose because this row exists to attribute, not to gate.
